name: AKU and WHO united against Ebola

content.text: The attendees were a mix of medical doctors with expertise in infectious diseases, epidemiologists and biosafety specialties. Dr Imran Nisar, Senior Instructor, Paediatrics and Child Health and Dr Sadia Shakoor, Assistant Professor, Pathology and Laboratory Medicine headed a team of AKU faculty which conducted the training.

The AKU faculty included: Dr Afia Zafar, Professor,  Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine; Dr Erum Khan, Associate Professor,  Department of Pathology  Laboratory Medicine; Dr Bushra Jamil, Associate professor, Department of Medicine and Dr Tahir Yousafzai, Senior Instructor, Department of Paediatrics and Child Health.
"We presented evidence-based lectures describing the current Ebola outbreak in West Africa, functions of a rapid response team and use of personal protection equipment," said Dr Shakoor.

The training was based on formulating a comprehensive strategy consisting of a package of interventions, i.e. case management; surveillance; identification and diagnosis of potential patients; laboratory service, safe burials and social awareness to control any future outbreak of Ebola.

"A cadre of trainers was developed for each country that will go back to their respective countries to train healthcare providers in Ebola rapid response in case of an outbreak,"" said Dr Nisar. The group will function at national and subnational levels and lead the development of efficient surveillance systems and orchestrate a rapid and efficient response if the need arises.

The participants worked on hypothetical scenarios and performed rapid risk assessment, investigated an outbreak, interviewed medical personnel, traced potential patients, and started an efficient response. The training also included role plays in which various facilitators acted as hospital manager, surveillance officers, paramedic staff and family members.

Dr Ezzeddine Mohsni, Acting Director, Communicable Diseases Prevention and Control, WHO, EMRO, expressed his satisfaction, "The training was indeed challenging; WHO appreciates its partners like AKU for their support and partnership. The impact of such capacity building efforts goes beyond Ebola response as it helps strengthen national capacities in the East Mediterranean Region to effectively respond to infectious disease outbreaks."

content.title: AKU and WHO united against Ebola
content.author: Muhammad Altamash
content.description: "The Aga Khan University conducted an Ebola Rapid Response Training as part of the World Health Organisation's 90 day action plan to strengthen national capacities in the wake of the recent Ebola outbreak. The training, held in Dubai from May 11-15, was attended by 50 professionals representing 10 Eastern Mediterranean Regional Office countries. The aim was to prevent Ebola outbreaks by maintaining surveillance and supporting vulnerable countries' preparation of effective action plans.
